instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment.
Cut the eggplants into 1 1/2-inch cubes. Toss them on the sheet with 3 tbsp of the olive oil and 3/4 tsp of the salt. Spread them in a single layer, using a second sheet if they're crowded.
Roast for 25 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the eggplant is soft and browned at the edges.
Meanwhile, dice the onion and mince the garlic. Drain and rinse the chickpeas, and pick the mint leaves off the stems.
Heat the other 2 tbsp of olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and smoked paprika and stir for 1 minute, until you can smell them.
Add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until it darkens.
Add the diced tomatoes with their juice, the chickpeas and 1 cup of water. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.

While that simmers, rinse the rice in a sieve. Put it in a small pot with 2 1/4 cups of water and the last 1/2 tsp of salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes. Leave it covered, off the heat, until you're ready to serve.
Add the roasted eggplant to the stew and cook for 10 minutes, until the sauce is thick.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in most of the mint leaves.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice, topped with the rest of the mint. Put the red pepper flakes on the table for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: No version of maghmour I could read has 20 or more ratings, and the trusted cook for this cuisine (RecipeTin Eats) has no maghmour, so the lead is the best-read real version, The Mountain Kitchen (5 from 3 votes, taken from the visible rating). All the versions roast or fry the eggplant, then simmer it into onion, tomato and chickpeas, and they differ on spice (smoked paprika and cayenne, plain paprika, or fresh mint) and on liquid. I followed the lead's roast-then-stew method with its smoked paprika, used the second source's fresh mint, left the cayenne out of the pot and moved heat to the table, and added rice so it eats as a dinner.
